title: Learned semantic coarse indexing for persistent-state retrieval
question: Can a learned semantic representation replace the hand-designed persistent-state index while preserving capability on held-out noisy queries and keeping the retained state shortlist bounded?
hypothesis: H_learned_index: a dual linear semantic encoder trained only on disjoint training codes will retrieve the correct persistent state item through a compact binary bucket index on the held-out evaluation codes, with indexed capability no worse than 0.05 below exhaustive at every registered H and seed.

arms.name: exhaustive
arms.intervention: scan all M=64 persistent state items and execute the exact candidate path

arms.name: learned_selective
arms.intervention: learned semantic dual encoder, binary bucket index, bounded Hamming probes, exact candidate index, execute four retained programs

endpoints.name: success_rate
endpoints.role: primary — aggregate output matches hidden environment truth

endpoints.name: state_target_retention
endpoints.role: secondary — correct state address survives learned index

endpoints.name: candidate_retention
endpoints.role: secondary — exact candidate bucket retains all four relevant programs

decision_rule.condition: learned_selective success_rate >= exhaustive success_rate - 0.05 at every registered H and seed; learned shortlist size <= 1; all four relevant programs are retained whenever the target state is retained
decision_rule.licenses: bounded support that the learned semantic state representation can cross the persistent retrieval boundary in this synthetic workload
decision_rule.does_not_license: general semantic memory, universal approximate nearest-neighbor retrieval, hardware speedup, natural-language reasoning, or the broad L4 C5 claim

decision_rule.condition: learned_selective success_rate < exhaustive success_rate - 0.05 in any registered H/seed or target-state retention fails
decision_rule.licenses: the registered learned semantic state-index mechanism does not preserve the preregistered capability boundary
decision_rule.does_not_license: that learned semantic indexing is impossible

held_constant: evaluation targets are CODEBOOK[:16]; training codes are CODEBOOK[16:64]
exactly four candidate programs are relevant to each evaluation state code
same fixed-work executor is used as TACOSM-C5-END-TO-END-001
exact candidate index remains the capability-matched control
prior C5 and REP evidence remains frozen
no evaluation address or gold target is used during index training

amendments.old_definition: build_task(seed, h, step) is called independently at each H, and its registered query noise bit therefore depends on H
amendments.new_definition: for each seed/step, the query and persistent-state task are generated once from build_task(seed, 64, step); candidate populations are then regenerated at each registered H while reusing that same query, target address, state values, and target code
amendments.rationale: The first CI run showed large capability differences by H. Because the original task builder computes the query flip from H, H changed the input distribution as well as candidate population size. The confirmatory run must isolate the intended H scaling variable.
amendments.discovered: After the first registered CI run, before any confirmatory result was declared.
amendments.affected: Query/noise generation only. Training/evaluation code split, state population, candidate relation, capability rule, encoder, index, shortlist, and executor are unchanged.
amendments.no_result_under_previous_version: The first CI run is retained as an exploratory diagnostic and is not a confirmatory result for this contract.
